submission.justification: Sensor-T3 is excluded: its measured hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2 is 82.0%, far below the hard 97% requirement (strong charge trapping, full depletion unreachable). Sensor-T2 meets efficiency (99.2%) but has clearly worse resolution at every thickness simulated (about 13.9-15.9 um). Sensor-T1 reaches 98.5% efficiency at end of life and gave the best resolution in our scan: 50 um 10.3, 100 um 9.27, 125 um 9.43, 150 um 8.68, 175 um 9.15, 200 um 9.34, 300 um 11.7 um. The minimum is at 150 um (8.68 um single-hit, unirradiated). Caveat: the irradiation campaign does not state the sensor thickness used for the 98.5% efficiency measurement, so the end-of-life efficiency at 150 um is inferred rather than directly measured; it should be confirmed with a 150 um irradiated sample before pre-production. The 150 um value (8.68 um) is also slightly below the 2025 summary's 9.0 um, so the simulation values should be cross-checked.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T1 (planar, standard pitch) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Hit efficiency >= 97% up to 2e16 neq/cm^2 (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: irradiation_testbeam_2026.md reports 98.5% for Sensor-T1 at 2e16 neq/cm^2. The thickness used for that measurement is not stated, so this is inferred for 150 um and should be confirmed.

requirements.requirement: Best possible single-hit spatial resolution in the innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Simulated T1 resolution at 150 um is 8.68 um, the lowest of all T1 thicknesses scanned (50-300 um) and well below T2 (13.9 um at 150 um). T3 would have been best (6.0 um in 2025 summary) but fails the efficiency requirement.
